readings.title: David Saves Keilah
readings.subtitle: Saul's Pursuit and David's Escape
readings.text: [1 Samuel 23:1] And they informed Daviḏ, saying, “See, the Philistines are fighting against Qe‛ilah, and they are plundering <dn>את</dn> the threshing-floors.” [2] So Daviḏ inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, saying, “Shall I go and strike these Philistines?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to Daviḏ, <dq>“Go and smite the Philistines, and save <dn>את</dn> Qe‛ilah.”</dq> [3] And Daviḏ’s men said to him, “See, we here in Yehuḏah are afraid. How much more, then, if we go to Qe‛ilah against the armies of the Philistines?” [4] And Daviḏ inquired of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> once again. And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> answered him and said, <dq>“Arise, go down to Qe‛ilah, for <dn>I</dn> am giving <dn>את</dn> the Philistines into your hand.”</dq> [5] So Daviḏ and his men went to Qe‛ilah and fought with the Philistines, and he led away <dn>את</dn> their livestock and struck them, a great smiting. Thus Daviḏ saved <dn>את</dn> the inhabitants of Qe‛ilah. [6] And it came to be, when Eḇyathar son of Aḥimeleḵ fled to Daviḏ at Qe‛ilah, that he went down with a shoulder garment in his hand. [7] And Sha’ul was informed that Daviḏ had gone to Qe‛ilah. Then Sha’ul said, “<dn>Elohim</dn> has estranged him into my hand, for he has shut himself in by entering a town that has gates and bars.” [8] And Sha’ul summoned <dn>את</dn> all the people to battle, to go down to Qe‛ilah to besiege Daviḏ and his men. [9] And Daviḏ knew that Sha’ul was plotting evil against him, and said to Eḇyathar the priest, “Bring the shoulder garment here.” [10] And Daviḏ said, “O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, <dn>Your</dn> servant has heard for certain that Sha’ul seeks to come to Qe‛ilah to destroy the city for my sake. [11] “Are the landowners of Qe‛ilah going to surrender me into his hand? Is Sha’ul coming down, as <dn>Your</dn> servant has heard? O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> <dn>Elohim</dn> of Yisra’ěl, I pray, let <dn>Your</dn> servant know.” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“He is coming down.”</dq> [12] And Daviḏ said, “Are the landowners of Qe‛ilah going to surrender me and <dn>את</dn> my men into the hand of Sha’ul?” And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said, <dq>“They are going to surrender you.”</dq> [13] Then Daviḏ and his men, about six hundred, arose and left Qe‛ilah and went wherever they could go. And Sha’ul was informed that Daviḏ had escaped from Qe‛ilah, and he ceased to go out. [14] And Daviḏ remained in the wilderness, in strongholds, and remained in the hill country in the Wilderness of Ziph. And Sha’ul sought him every day, but <dn>Elohim</dn> did not give him into his hand.

readings.title: The Wilderness of Ziph and Maon
readings.subtitle: Jonathan's Covenant and Saul's Diversion
readings.text: [15] And Daviḏ saw that Sha’ul had come out to seek <dn>את</dn> his life while Daviḏ was in the Wilderness of Ziph at Ḥoresh. [16] And Yehonathan, Sha’ul’s son, arose and went to Daviḏ at Ḥoresh and strengthened <dn>את</dn> his hand in <dn>Elohim</dn>, [17] and said to him, “Do not fear, for the hand of Sha’ul my father is not going to find you, and you are to reign over Yisra’ěl, and I am to be next to you. Even my father Sha’ul knows that.” [18] And they made a covenant before <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>. And Daviḏ remained at Ḥoresh while Yehonathan went to his own house. [19] And the Ziphites came up to Sha’ul at Giḇ‛ah, saying, “Is Daviḏ not hiding with us in strongholds Ḥoresh, in the hill of Ḥaḵilah, which is on the south of the wasteland? [20] “And now, O sovereign, by all the desire of your being, come down, come down, and our part is to surrender him into the sovereign’s hand.” [21] And Sha’ul said, “Blessed are you of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for you have sympathy with me. [22] “Please go, prepare yet further and find out and see <dn>את</dn> the place where his hide-out is, who has seen him there. For I am told that he is very cunning. [23] “So look, and learn all about the hiding places where he hides. And you shall come back to me with certainty, then I shall go with <dn>את</dn> you. And it shall be, if he is in the land, that I shall search for him throughout all the clans of Yehuḏah.” [24] And they rose up and went to Ziph before Sha’ul, while Daviḏ and his men were in the Wilderness of Ma‛on, in the desert plain on the south of the wasteland. [25] And Sha’ul and his men went to seek him, and they informed Daviḏ, so he went down to the rock, and remained in the Wilderness of Ma‛on. And when Sha’ul heard this, he pursued Daviḏ in the Wilderness of Ma‛on. [26] And Sha’ul went on one side of the mountain, and Daviḏ and his men on the other side of the mountain. And Daviḏ was hurrying to get away from Sha’ul, for Sha’ul and his men were surrounding Daviḏ and his men to take them. [27] Then a messenger came to Sha’ul, saying, “Hurry and come, for the Philistines have invaded <dn>את</dn> the land!” [28] So Sha’ul turned back from pursuing Daviḏ, and went against the Philistines. Therefore they called that place Sela Hammaḥleqoth. [29] And Daviḏ went up from there and remained in strongholds at Ěn Geḏi.

readings.title: David Spares Saul's Life
readings.subtitle: The Cave at En Gedi
readings.text: [1 Samuel 24:1] And it came to be, when Sha’ul had returned from pursuing the Philistines, that it was reported to him, saying, “See, Daviḏ is in the Wilderness of Ěn Geḏi.” [2] So Sha’ul took three thousand chosen men from all Yisra’ěl, and went to seek <dn>את</dn> Daviḏ and his men on the Rocks of the Wild Goats. [3] And he came to the sheepfolds, on the way, and there was a cave. And Sha’ul went in to relieve <dn>את</dn> himself. Now Daviḏ and his men were sitting in the sides of the cave. [4] And the men of Daviḏ said to him, “See, the day of which <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> said to you, ‘See, <dn>I</dn> am giving <dn>את</dn> your enemy into your hand, and you shall do to him as it seems good to you!’ ” And Daviḏ arose and gently cut off <dn>את</dn> a corner of Sha’ul’s robe. [5] And it came to be afterward that the heart of Daviḏ struck him because he had cut <dn>את</dn> the robe of Sha’ul. [6] So he said to his men, “Far be it from me, by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, that I should do <dn>את</dn> this matter to my master, anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, to stretch out my hand against him, for he is the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.” [7] And Daviḏ dispersed <dn>את</dn> his servants with words, and did not allow them to rise against Sha’ul. And Sha’ul rose up from the cave and went on his way. [8] And afterward Daviḏ arose and went out of the cave, and called out to Sha’ul, saying, “My master the sovereign!” And when Sha’ul looked behind him, Daviḏ bowed with his face to the earth, and did obeisance. [9] And Daviḏ said to Sha’ul, “Why do you listen to <dn>את</dn> the words of men who say, ‘See, Daviḏ seeks to do you evil’? [10] “See, this day your eyes have seen that <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> gave you today into my hand in the cave, and one said to kill you. But my eye pardoned you, and I said, ‘I do not stretch out my hand against my master, for he is the anointed of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>.’ [11] “And my father, see! Yes, see <dn>את</dn> the corner of your robe in my hand! For in that I cut off <dn>את</dn> the corner of your robe, and did not kill you, know and see that there is neither evil nor rebellion in my hand, and I have not sinned against you, while you are hunting <dn>את</dn> my life to take it. [12] “Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> judge between you and me, and let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> revenge me on you, but my hand is not against you. [13] “As the proverb of the ancients says, ‘Wrong comes from the wrongdoer.’ But my hand is not against you. [14] “After whom has the sovereign of Yisra’ěl come out? Whom do you pursue? A dead dog? A flea? [15] “And <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> shall be judge, and rightly rule between you and me, and see and plead <dn>את</dn> my case, and rightly rule me out of your hand.” [16] And it came to be, when Daviḏ had ended speaking <dn>את</dn> these words to Sha’ul, that Sha’ul said, “Is this your voice, my son Daviḏ?” So Sha’ul lifted up his voice and wept. [17] And he said to Daviḏ, “You are more righteous than I, for you have rewarded me with good, whereas I have rewarded you with evil. [18] “And you have shown today how <dn>את</dn> you have done good to me, for when <dn>את</dn> <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> surrendered me into your hand you did not kill me. [19] “For if a man finds <dn>את</dn> his enemy, shall he let him get away safely? And let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> reward you with good for what you have done to me today. [20] “And now look, I know that you shall certainly reign, and that the reign of Yisra’ěl shall be established in your hand. [21] “And now, swear to me by <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> that you do not cut off <dn>את</dn> my seed after me, nor destroy <dn>את</dn> my name from my father’s house.” [22] And Daviḏ swore to Sha’ul. Then Sha’ul went home, and Daviḏ and his men went up to the stronghold.

readings.title: A Prayer for Deliverance
readings.subtitle: Trusting in the Name of Elohim
readings.text: [Psalm 54:1] O <dn>Elohim</dn>, save me by <dn>Your</dn> Name, And rightly rule me by <dn>Your</dn> might. [2] Hear my prayer, O <dn>Elohim</dn>; Give ear to the words of my mouth. [3] For strangers have risen up against me, And cruel men have sought after my life; They have not set <dn>Elohim</dn> before them. Selah. [4] See, <dn>Elohim</dn> is my helper; <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> is with those who sustain my life. [5] <dn>He</dn> repays evil to my enemies. Cut them off in <dn>Your</dn> truth. [6] Voluntarily I slaughter to <dn>You</dn>; I praise <dn>Your</dn> Name, O <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, for it is good. [7] For <dn>He</dn> has delivered me out of all distress; And my eye has looked upon my enemies.
